title: Security
description: Can threat-model, authenticate, authorize and keep secrets out of Git — and can map a fix to an OWASP-shaped abuse case on a system they own.

levels.name: Foundation
levels.description: Can draw a DFD with numbered trust boundaries, classify each crossing store or flow, and list an OWASP-mapped threat without committing a secret — under written guidance.

levels.name: Apprentice
levels.description: Can store passwords with a dedicated hash, prove logout rejects a replayed session, and move a secret from Git to the environment with a scanner that fails on a planted dummy.

levels.name: Practitioner
levels.description: Can independently prove object-level authorization with a test that user A cannot read user B's object, distinguish 401 from 403 on the same route, and write a residual-risk register with open, mitigated or accepted.

levels.name: Journeyman
levels.description: Can review a real application diff with severity, OWASP or CWE, and must-fix versus non-blocking; apply or record residual risk; and name one horizontal and one vertical privilege failure from that system.

levels.name: Mastery Evidence
levels.description: Can review another apprentice's threat model or auth fix, name a checklist item that does not map to a trust-boundary crossing (or a secret left in history), and teach when to trust a server-side check over a hidden UI control on an unfamiliar app.
